newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean defector reported ready to die in China.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector reported ready to die in China.

text.p: The highest-ranking North Korean to betray his Stalinist homeland began his fourth day marooned inside a Seoul embassy mission in Beijing on Saturday, and was reported to have said he was ready to die there.

A North Korean delegation arrived in Beijing, but the identities of its members were unknown and it was unclear if they planned to discuss the defection of Hwang Jang-yop, who turned up at the mission on Wednesday with an aide.
A North Korean embassy vehicle whisked the team members from Beijing's international airport.

Pyongyang students and officials continued their vigil outside the South Korean compound, prevented from getting too close by a cordon of Chinese police officers and spikes laid across approaches to the building to stop cars.
Hwang has become the focus of a Cold War tussle between the two Koreas, arch-enemies since their 1950-53 war ended only in a truce.
China is playing for time as it agonises over a diplomatic quandary -- how to usher Hwang out of Beijing without offending its old socialist comrade or new capitalist friend.
Hwang, the scholarly architect of North Korea's national ideology of Juche, or self-reliance, was reported to be adamant he wanted to go to South Korea -- and nowhere else.
"I will die here if my determination to go to South Korea cannot be realised," Hwang said in a statement released by Seoul authorities.
"I want to make it clear that South Korea is the place where I want to go, and I will not go to any third country."

China has signalled its annoyance with South Korea's loudhailer diplomacy, and a flurry of diplomatic activity on Friday in Singapore, where Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen was attending Asia-Europe talks, failed to break the deadlock.
Ryu Kwang-sok, director-general of Asia-Pacific Affairs Bureau at Seoul's Foreign Ministry, said China wanted a low-key approach to resolving the crisis.
"I have the impression that China wants to resolve the row with Hwang quietly," he said.
But he added: "We will pour all our strength into negotiations with China."
South Korea's trade promotion agency said on Saturday it had instructed its 106 overseas missions to heighten vigilance against possible North Korean attack.
Japan has made clear it does not want to play middleman in the affair, and the United States also said it would stay clear of tricky negotations that could drag on for some time.

State Department Nicholas Burns said although Hwang's case was "of enormous interest to us", the United States had made no attempt to get involved and regarded it as a matter for South Korea and China to resolve.
The United States said it saw no likelihood the defection would affect planned talks on the future of the Korean peninsula.

"We don't believe that this particular incident in Beijing is going to have an effect on the issues that are of primary concern to us," a State Department spokesman said, referring to Korean peace talks and an accord under which Pyongyang agreed to freeze its nuclear weapons programme.
Washington and Seoul have been trying to arrange a joint briefing for North Korean officials on the proposal for talks involving the two Koreas, the United States and China.

Pyongyang has already twice postponed the briefing, due to be held in New York, because of its failure so far to negotiate a grain import deal with U.S. trader Cargill Inc. to help alleviate its famine.
